title: Design System: What Are We Watching

display.purpose: The SURPRISE ME key: wide black italic, 90s retail sign lettering.

headline.purpose: Film title on the sleeve: black ultra-condensed caps.

title.purpose: Sign-board section plaques, yellow, trailed by a fading rule.

body.purpose: The film's one-line take on the sleeve insert, max 62ch.

print-label.purpose: Year, director and cast lines printed on the sleeve.

label.purpose: Keys, chips and tags: condensed caps.

osd.purpose: VT323 on the tube and the VCR window only.

shadows.name: main-key
shadows.purpose: The big yellow key at rest.

shadows.name: main-key-pressed
shadows.purpose: The big yellow key pressed (3px travel).

shadows.name: chip
shadows.purpose: Blue genre chip keys at rest.

shadows.name: chip-on
shadows.purpose: A chip pressed in and latched (yellow).

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Sign board resting on the counter.

shadows.name: recess
shadows.purpose: VFD window set into the counter.

shadows.name: vfd-glow
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for VFD phosphor; the only UI glow.

shadows.name: highlight-overlay-scale
shadows.purpose: The Moulded Plastic highlight scale: sheen .07, dark-key/case edge .12-.14, wells .2, blue-key edge .25-.34, yellow-key and sticker edge .55-.65, die-cut edges .75-.85.

shadows.name: shade-overlay-scale
shadows.purpose: The Moulded Plastic shade scale: input well .18, lips .25-.35, contact shadows .4-.6, case inner edge and hinge groove .65-.7, panel drops and VFD recess .8-.9.

shadows.name: bloom
shadows.purpose: three.js bloom on emissive surfaces: tube, VFD, neon; dropped on slow devices.

motion.name: channel-change
motion.purpose: Static between picks; 30% torn colour bars, else snow with CH 03.

motion.name: dial-detent
motion.value: 30deg per pick, exponential approach k=22/s with overshoot
motion.purpose: VHF dial turns one detent per channel change; instant when reduced.

motion.name: sleeve-settle
motion.value: opacity 340ms ease-out, transform 460ms ease-out (8px), blur 2px; force reveal 1400ms

motion.name: stage-fade
motion.purpose: Canvas fades in when the set is ready.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No transitions, sway, drift, hum, tracking tear or sleeve blur; dial jumps; render on change only.

narrative.overview:
The page is a place, not a panel. A Blender-built silver 70s portable TV sits on a 90s VCR on a rental-store counter, lit in three.js in front of an out-of-focus Cycles plate of the store: face-out tapes on white shelving, blue section headers, a pink VIDEO and cyan OPEN LATE neon. The tube is the product's voice. The name WHAT ARE WE WATCHING lives on its VCR-blue idle screen, a pick is a channel change (half a second of snow or torn colour bars, one detent of the VHF dial, a static "shh"), and the film then plays on the tube like a tape.

Everything the hand touches sits in front of that scene and is made of the counter's own stuff: a blue sign board with yellow plaques, chunky bevelled plastic keys, fluorescent decade stickers, a VFD count window glowing cyan, and the back of a rental case (pebbled black clamshell over a printed insert under clear vinyl) that carries the film's words. Two worlds are composed and never blended: the lit 3D world behind, and the tactile retail-plastic world in front. The period line is pre-Frutiger-Aero: plastic, print and phosphor, never frosted glass or glossy bubbles.

Density is operational. The pick, the filters and the facts stay one glance away; the theatre happens on the tube, not by hiding controls.
keyCharacteristics: A lit 3D set (TV, VCR, counter, returned tapes) in front of a baked, bokeh'd store plate; one camera frames every layout.
Rental blue and sticker yellow carry the whole UI; VFD cyan and neon pink/cyan are light sources, not fills.
Archivo in two voices (wide black italic signage, condensed caps print); VT323 only on the tube and the VCR.
Physical keys: gradient plastic, inset top highlight, inset bottom lip, soft drop; they travel down 1-3px when pressed.
Every raster is procedural Blender output that carries its own provenance.

rules.name: The Light Source Rule
rules.body: Only things that emit light glow: the tube, the VFD, the neon. Glow (text-shadow, bloom) never lands on a panel, key or type that is paint or print.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Press Rule
rules.body: Among the controls, a Sticker Yellow surface means "this is the thing to press" or "this is pressed". Elsewhere yellow is signage and print: plaque rules, pinstripes, labels, the year and billing lines; never body copy.

rules.name: The Two Blues Rule
rules.body: Rental Blue is the store; VCR Blue is the tube. Do not swap them.

rules.name: The Tube Font Rule
rules.body: VT323 lives only on the tube (the OSD and idle screen canvases) and the VCR window. Anything printed or signed is Archivo.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Wide italic black is for signage you press or read across the room; condensed caps is for print you read up close. Reading text (the take, the actor field) is plain sentence-case Archivo. Do not invent a third display voice.

rules.name: The Moulded Plastic Rule
rules.body: A pressable surface has a crisp inset top highlight, a crisp inset bottom lip and a soft blurred drop; it travels 1-3px down on press. Outer drop shadows are always blurred; no flat pressables.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop blur, no frosted or translucent panels. The only transparency is the clear vinyl sheen over the sleeve insert, a single faint diagonal band.

dos: **Do** keep the TV the first thing seen: centre on desktop, pinned across the top when stacked, with the yellow key directly under it.
**Do** make every pressable a moulded plastic key with a top highlight, bottom lip and soft drop, travelling 1-3px on press.
**Do** keep VT323 on the tube and the VCR only; Archivo wide black italic for signage, condensed caps for print.
**Do** put glow only on things that emit light: the tube, the VFD, the neon.
**Do** give each decade its own fluorescent sticker ink with black type and a white die-cut edge.
**Do** draw icons as SVG paths in the page and as canvas paths on the tube.
**Do** build new rasters in Blender, ship them beside index.html under the content hash, and embed their provenance.
**Do** evoke the era only: no real store's name, logo or marks.
donts: **Don't** use frosted glass, backdrop blur, glossy bubbles or any Frutiger-Aero finish.
**Don't** put a dark app card on a flat page; controls sit in the store world, on the counter.
**Don't** use hard, unblurred outer drop shadows; depth comes from the lit set and the moulded key's inset lip and soft drop.
**Don't** set UI, signage or printed text in VT323.
**Don't** give a non-pressable control or panel a Sticker Yellow surface.
**Don't** use text glyphs or emoji as icons.
